about: Conformance vectors for the assaio exec-plugin protocols. Each vector is one document exactly as a plugin would write it, plus the verdict assaio's own boundary gives it. Run them in your plugin's CI without the assaio binary: feed `doc` to your decoder and assert `accept`; when `accept` is false, your rejection reason should mention `expect`. assaio's own tests are driven by these same files (internal/plugin/conformance_test.go), so a vector that stops describing the boundary fails assaio's build rather than yours.
description: What a metric plugin writes after its handshake when invoked as `<command> describe`.

vectors.why: the smallest honest declaration: one capability, no narrowing
columns inside a section, including the nested step list where the bytes are
grain and population are columns, so both are ordinary predicates
declaring everything is allowed, and is what a protocol-3 plugin's migration looks like
an empty declaration must not mean the pre-4 default of everything
a plugin that reads nothing has nothing to report
the capability set is closed; a typo must fail loudly, not withhold silently
a capability named twice is a declaration its author did not read back
a projection over a section that does not exist projects nothing, silently
projecting a section you did not ask for cannot be honoured either way
a column projected away and one that never existed read identically on arrival

vectors.expect: omit the section to receive it whole
vectors.why: an empty column list is ambiguous between no columns and every column
a predicate names a column, and a bare section name names none
same reason as an unknown projection: a filter nobody applies is a filter that lies
dropping steps from inside a sequence leaves its ordinals describing a set nobody declared
a predicate is set membership over a label, never a comparison over a count
a predicate admitting nothing sends an empty section that reads as an empty window
a misspelled key that decodes to nothing is a declaration its author believes they made
exactly one document follows the handshake
the YAML shape of the old config key is the mistake a migrating author makes first
